summary: Compare medtech knowledge base tools, then learn what to evaluate and how to centralize support answers for secure, regulated workflows at scale.
body_markdown:
When a support team member solves an integration issue, the context isn’t automatically shared with the rest of the team. If the next person gets the same question from a different department and doesn’t know where to find the answer, then they have to start the investigation over.


Repeating work makes it harder to give customers consistent answers quickly, especially as ticket volume increases. Knowledge base tools can turn those answers into shared, searchable instructions. That way, the same documentation can support troubleshooting, onboarding, and collaboration across departments.


This guide explains how to compare knowledge base tools for medtech around the industry’s specific compliance and access needs.


## What’s knowledge base software for support teams?


A[knowledge base](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-software-2025) , or knowledge database software, is a centralized platform for storing and organizing company information. It gives your team a place to manage institutional intelligence like answers, best practices, and troubleshooting steps.


Say a customer asks how to set up user permissions for their laboratory in your reporting software. Your onboarding team can search for and use a how-to guide to walk them through setup. When that customer adds another lab location, the support team can use the same instructions instead of asking the implementation lead to explain them again.


Your knowledge base platform should account for two audiences:


- **Internal knowledge bases.** Your team uses runbooks, escalation instructions, and technical explanations to investigate issues. New team members can access the same processes as experienced teammates.
- **Customer-facing and AI-powered knowledge bases.** Customers use approved articles to troubleshoot independently. Your team’s AI agents can retrieve or summarize those articles.


Sharing the same topic doesn’t mean sharing the same instructions. Access and response rules need to preserve the boundary between sensitive and public information. That limit is especially important in medtech, where your customers’ information is also regulated under laws like HIPAA.


For example, a[customer knowledge base](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-knowledge-base) might explain the checks a hospital administrator can safely perform and when to contact your team. Your internal integration runbook includes diagnostic steps that need elevated permissions for the same query that the customer doesn’t need to see.


## How to evaluate and choose the right platform for medtech


Generate KB article for Pylon


Access controls and content approval matter more than search convenience. An answer that appears instantly still slows the process if your team has to check whether it’s current and appropriate for the customer.


Start by defining what data the platform will handle. In the United States, if a cloud provider processes customer health records or sensitive patient information on behalf of a HIPAA-covered entity, they’ll need to provide an appropriate business associate agreement (BAA). A BAA is a formal contract that defines how they process that electronic protected health information (ePHI) and how they plan to keep that information secure. They will also need to show they’re compliant with all applicable HIPAA rules; a BAA doesn’t automatically make every configuration or connected workflow compliant.


Use that scope to compare knowledge base platforms against practical tests:


- **Security and compliance scope.** Find the BAA and which features it covers, then compare those to your customer with the highest compliance needs. Review any additional audit log, access revocation, and data processing features to find compliance gaps.
- **Centralized content and version control.** Find an approved integration guide, then review its revision history and identify who each change came from. Look for any visible outdated product version information.
- **Permissions and cross-team access.** Let support and dev teams collaborate on a knowledge base article, then check the customer side to ensure they only see permitted content, not the internal conversation.
- **AI search and answer accuracy.** Search for a known answer to a troubleshooting question and compare the AI response to the right steps. Then, see how the system handles the same process without an approved answer.
- **Workflow guidance and collaboration.** Move a resolved issue into an article draft, collect feedback, and look at what happens to the context after publication.
- **Volume capacity and analytics tools.** Review search performance at your average volume and identify unanswered searches or repeat requests.
- **Multilingual access.** Compare translated instructions after the source article changes.
- **Integrations.** Check if the platform can retrieve approved answers from your help desk or Slack and use customer context without exposing sensitive information.


Most importantly, inspect how each tool presents metadata about[knowledge base articles](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-articles-what-they-are-how-to-make-them-effective) . A revision timestamp tells you when text changed. Your team still needs a clear indication of which release the instructions support and whether the right reviewer approved them.


## 4 great knowledge base tools for medtech support teams


The best starting point for your team depends on your priority: shared documentation, clinical guidance, or a knowledge base connected to customer support workflows. These four platforms serve different stages of that process.

### General-purpose platforms support teams already use


If your small team already uses a broad support platform, you may be able to build on a familiar interface and existing context instead of adopting another place to look for answers.


#### Confluence


Atlassian’s knowledge base tool,[Confluence](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence) , keeps technical documentation in shared spaces, with page history that lets your team inspect earlier versions. For a medtech integration team, that history can help explain what changed after an update or new release.


**Best for:** Teams that want to build on an existing internal documentation library.


**Watch out for:** The Free plan doesn’t let you customize page permissions, which matter when instructions need to stay internal. BAA eligibility is a separate limitation — Atlassian only offers BAAs for eligible Confluence Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans, not Free plans or trials.


#### SharePoint


When document review is central to your workflow, consider Microsoft’s[SharePoint](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/sharepoint/collaboration) tool. Its versioning and draft controls can separate revisions from approved content. That way, you can configure who sees drafts and who can only access approved material.


**Best for:** Teams that need document libraries with defined reviewer roles and permissions.


**Watch out for:** When you enable content approval in a library that already contains files, SharePoint automatically marks those existing files as approved. Review the existing library after migration before treating its approval labels as evidence that the instructions are up to date.


### Support and healthcare-focused platforms


Some clinical teams need to access their institution’s guidance alongside information about your medtech product in their workflows.


#### C8 Health


[C8 Health](https://c8health.com/) ’s clinical knowledge platform brings clinical and health systems’ operational guides together. Its Panda AI answers questions from the institution’s vetted knowledge base with linked source citations.


**Best for:** Organizations that need clinicians to find institution-specific guidance.


**Watch out for:** A knowledge management system in healthcare may serve a different audience from your medtech support team. Test customer access, ticket handling, and product-version workflows separately before treating the clinical platform as a fit for B2B support.


If customer support is your main use case but your customers have strict compliance requirements, consider how a healthcare-focused workflow could integrate with[support-focused knowledge base software](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-software-support-teams-2025) first.

## FAQ


### What’s the best AI knowledge base tool?


It depends on your customers’ legal requirements and compliance workflows. Pylon’s agentic AI doesn’t replace support team members, so people can review content and make sure it meets all the right rules. Prioritize source-backed answers, permissions, and a practical way to turn new resolutions into maintained documentation without exposing sensitive account information or ePHI.


### Which AI knowledge base is best for medtech?


Confirm your customers’ data handling and approval requirements before making a choice. For more general B2B product support, try Pylon for its efficient agentic AI and balanced controls. For institutional clinical guidance, start with healthcare-focused tools.


### How can AI improve medtech knowledge bases?


AI agents can help team members and customers find relevant articles, identify missing answers, and draft documentation from resolved issues for a more robust knowledge base and faster time to resolution. Your team still needs to verify the content and decide which information customers can access.


### What should I look for in an AI knowledge base?


Look for:


- Citations
- Role-based access
- Clear ownership
- Revision controls
- Integrations with your current support tools
- How the AI responds when approved documentation is missing or outdated
